items.meta_title: VPN Protocols: UDP, TCP and QUIC | VpnHood!
items.meta_description: Switch between UDP, TCP and QUIC to suit the network you are on, and block QUIC when it gets in the way of video. Available in VpnHood!
items.title: Protocols
items.lead: A VPN protocol defines how your data travels between your device and the server. Switch between them to suit the network you are on.
items.shot_alt: The Protocols screen in the VpnHood! app
items.platforms: Android, iOS, Windows and Linux. QUIC availability varies by platform.
items.diagram_desc: In Cloak Mode, an app's QUIC cannot go as a stream, so it goes as packets in one long tunnel, and a network filter can spot that tunnel's bumpy shape and drop it. With Block QUIC, apps switch to TCP, and each connection goes in a smooth tunnel of its own that looks like web browsing to the filter.
items.diagram_off_result: Its shape can give it away
items.diagram_caption: In Cloak Mode, block QUIC for smooth tunnels
items.how_desc: UDP is the lightweight option and usually the fastest, though some networks restrict it. TCP is the reliable one: slower in theory, but it gets through where UDP does not. QUIC is a modern protocol over UDP, faster again where it is allowed.
items.when_desc: Switch when a network is slow or refusing to connect. Try UDP first for speed and TCP when something is in the way. Blocking QUIC makes apps fall back to standard streaming, which can improve video playback in Cloak Mode.
items.cost_desc: Nothing. The protocol switches on the live connection, so you can try another the moment one underperforms without dropping the tunnel.
